subject: Film & Cinema
title: Tinnitus and Disorientation Effects
description: A quick, practical guide to Tinnitus and Disorientation Effects.

hook.text: After an explosion in Saving Private Ryan, all sound drops to a ringing tone. You feel the blast.

buildup.text: Filmmakers simulate tinnitus to put audiences inside a character's disoriented state.

discovery.text: This technique — muffling the world to a high-pitched ring — triggers visceral empathy.

twist.text: It's become so common in war films that it risks feeling like a cliché.

climax.text: When used with restraint, it remains one of cinema's most immersive sound effects.

punchline.text: The ringing puts you inside the pain.

quiz.question: What does simulated tinnitus achieve in film?
options: It places the audience inside a character's disoriented state
